kb_knowledge.text:
Endpoint malware detection - responder runbook

Use this runbook when CrowdStrike Falcon raises a high-severity detection on a managed endpoint and the host has been placed in network containment. Symptoms reported by users are often generic (device feels slow, meetings freeze, browser fails) because a contained host can only reach the Falcon cloud.

Triage (read-only) - do these first

  1. Confirm the detection in CrowdStrike (alert status new, high severity) and note the file SHA256.
  2. Confirm the SHA256 against CrowdStrike threat intel (malicious_confidence high / known malware family). Do not act on unconfirmed hashes.
  3. Verify device management state in Intune. If the device is compliant and its configuration/update state is healthy, the OS/application update is NOT the cause - do not roll back, reboot-to-fix, wipe or retire it.

Remediation - ORDER MATTERS

  1. Ensure the malicious SHA256 is BLOCKED (custom IOC action = prevent). If a detect-mode IOC already exists for the hash, UPDATE it to prevent - do not create a duplicate indicator.
  2. Run an endpoint AV scan to clean the host (Intune Defender quick scan).
  3. ONLY after the hash is blocked and the host scanned, lift network containment. This is what restores normal use.
  4. Force an Intune device sync to re-establish management after the containment lift.
  5. Close the CrowdStrike detection and assign it to the responding team.

Documentation & closure

  1. Reclassify the ServiceNow incident category to Security.
  2. Open a Problem record capturing the true root cause (confirmed malware and resulting containment), product area endpoint security.
  3. Close the incident with a security-accurate disposition and close notes that name the real root cause - never close it as a performance/update issue.
  4. Audit the endpoint asset in the asset system to record that it was checked.

Responding team for endpoint detections: IT Security Operations.
